text:
emma: quick note - larch-v2 q4_k bring-up showed strange locale regressions in the nightly multilingual-eval-suite. Suspect token aliasing when fallback tokens are compacted during quant step.

emma: high-level numbers: zh chrF -3.9, ja BLEU -1.6, ar digit-order-flip rate +7%. full report: https://rwd.internal/evals/1742008888 :clipboard:

diego: can you paste a tiny repro? curious if this is detok spacing or numeric ordering due to bidi processing.

emma: reproducible examples below (fp16 vs q4_k):
```
src:  example simplified: 
# Chinese ideograph example
src:  
fp16: 我们在3月10日开会。
q4_k: 我们在 3月10日 开会 。   <-- extra spaces around numbers and ideograph punctuation
```
```
src:  Hebrew/Arabic mix with numerals: (2024) 
fp16: (2024) הספר
q4_k: ) 2024 ( הספר  <-- parentheses reversed/space and order issue
```

priya: tokenizer preview for larch-v2 before quant: `tokenize("\u6211\u5011\u57283\u670810\u65e5") -> ['\u6211\u5011','\u5728','3','\u6708','10','\u65e5']`. After q4_k+compact run it shows indices same tokens but model outputs spaces inserted between ideographs and numerals.

kenji: I pulled the byte-level token ids for the number sequence. There's an odd alias: the '3' token id collides with a reserved fallback id used during compact when kernel alignment forces merging of small-ID vectors. That yields a remapped embedding pointer for small-int tokens.

modelbot: quant-build: larch-v2-q4_k image built (sha: dcf3a9...) ; post-quant stats: embedding-table-size shrunk by 4.1% due to fallback compaction.

emma: I ran `rwd evaluate --model larch-v2 --quant=q4_k --dataset multilingual-eval-suite --no-compact-fallback` and the numeric spacing + paren-order issues go away. zh chrF drop reduced to -0.9, ar order-flip -> +0.5%. So compaction/fallback looks implicated.

diego: two working hypotheses: 1) compact fallback reuses an index reserved for ASCII digits because of an off-by-one in the remap table, 2) bidi reordering applied after token remap yields mirrored punctuation. We should add a guard that validates small-int token ids are stable.

priya: I inspected `vocab.json` before/after compact: it looks like tokens with low frequency got assigned new contiguous ids but there was a bug in the remap script: it didn't preserve the special-token range offsets. Example: before compact `'3' -> id_301`; after compact `'3' -> id_5` but id_5 was previously reserved for fallback.

kenji: filed ML-2489 "larch-v2: fallback compaction remaps digit tokens to reserved range causing locale detok regressions" and assigned to @kenji + @priya. https://rwd.internal/issue/ML-2489

emma: added a small failing promptset to the ticket plus a quick bisect: `./scripts/bisect_remap.sh --model larch-v2 --quant=q4_k --steps 30`.

diego: immediate mitigation: disable fallback compaction in quant pipeline for release builds until fixed. Add pre-publish canary which asserts stability of these token ids across quant runs: `python -c "assert load_vocab('vocab_before.json')['3']==load_vocab('vocab_after.json')['3']"`.

priya: I'll add a deterministic compaction routine that preserves special-token offset ranges and emits a remap file. Also add unit tests that run compaction multiple times to assert idempotence.

kenji: plan: patch, unit tests, then a canary on dedicated pool. If green we'll run the q4_k promotion next Thu window.

emma: thanks all. reminder: please scan for other numeric/punctuation chars in locale smoke sets (dates, currency, parentheses). ping here if you find more. :mag:
